newsitem.title: POLAND: SUDZUCKER TO BUY POLISH SUGAR REFINERY.
newsitem.headline: SUDZUCKER TO BUY POLISH SUGAR REFINERY.

text.p: German sugar company Sudzucker Gruppe will pay 49 million zlotys for a 38.2 percent stake in Poland's Ropczyce sugar refinery, Ropczyce said in a statment on Friday.
It said that Sudzucker had won a tender for the Ropczyce stake after it agreed to pay seven zlotys for each of the firm's seven million new shares.

After the completion of the sale, expected by the end of March, Sudzucker will hold 38.2 percent of shares in the company, the state-owned sugar firm Lubelsko-Malopolska Spolka Cukrowa> will have 31.5 percent and the state treasury -- 30.2 percent.
Out of the 49 million zlotys invested by Sudzucker seven million zlotys will be used to increase Ropczyce's capital and 42 million will be earmarked for raising its reserve capital.

Ropczyce, based in the south-eastern town of the same name, said the deal with Europe's biggest beet sugar producer Sudzucker would end its financial problems, enable it to pay debts and modernise production.
Ropczyce, which has not released earnings figures, produced 58,000 tonnes of sugar last year.

Other bidders for Ropczyce, one of Poland's biggest sugar refineries, included Rolimpex , Denmark's Danisco A/S , France's Eridania Beghin-Say , the Netherlands' Cosun and Britain's Tate and Lyle and British Sugar. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
